# THE FROZEN FIXTURE NEGATIVE-CONTROL CONTRACT.
# Each control MUTATES a COPY of the canonical fixture and then RUNS
# the REAL PolyC verifier binary against the mutated copy.  A control
# passes only when the real verifier returns a NON-ZERO exit code, i.e.
# when it actually REJECTED the mutated fixture.
# A control that merely asserts that a check exists would be vacuous.
# The verifier is EXECUTED and its exit code is the verdict.
# The mutated copies live under the build directory.  The tracked
# canonical fixture is NEVER touched.

column1: # THE EIGHT CONTROLS ARE MANDATORY (ACT section 6.7).
# THE CONTROLS MUST BE EXECUTABLE, NOT ASSERTED
# Each control runs the REAL verifier binary and requires a NON-ZERO
# exit code.  A control that only asserted "a check exists" would be
# vacuous and would pass even if the verifier were broken.
# EACH CONTROL MUST ALSO NAME ITS INTENDED FAILURE REASON
# ACT section 10 requires that the negative-control dispositions
# include the intended failure reason, not merely a nonzero verifier
# exit.  So each control records the verifier output lines that
# establish WHY it rejected, and the control passes only when the
# expected reason class is present.
# NC-06 IS THE ROW-COUNT-PRESERVING CONTROL
# NC-06 is deliberately the hardest control: it removes a row AND
# replaces it with a different row, so the total row count is
# UNCHANGED.  A verifier that only compared the row count would
# accept it.  The fixture's own id set, the accepted-token coverage and
# the semantic comparison each catch it.
# WHICH VERIFIERS RUN
#   integrity  -> build/parser-slice05-fixture-integrity
#   differential-> build/parser-slice05-differential
# The differential is required for the semantic controls (NC-05,
# NC-06, NC-07, NC-08) because the integrity witness checks the
# FIXTURE'S OWN internal consistency, while the differential checks the
# fixture against the REAL legacy oracle and the REAL PolyC
# component.
